title: Establishment of a Surgically-induced Model in Mice to Investigate the Protective Role of Progranulin in Osteoarthritis
protocol: Select 8-12 weeks old male C57BL/6 mice with a body weight of approximately 25 g for surgery.
Anesthetize the animals through intraperitoneal injection of a cocktail containing both xylazine (5 mg/kg) and ketamine (40 mg/kg).
Shave the knee with razors.
Surgically drape the animal.
Sterilize the surgical site with betadine and alcohol (3x).
Cover the mouse eyes with ointment.
Make a 1 cm longitudinal medial para-patellar incision to expose knee joint.
Open the knee joint gently through lateral dislocation of the patella and patellar ligament.
Cut the knee joint capsule longitudinally through the medial para-patellar incision.
Dissect knee joint capsule with forceps.
Grab the distal part of hind paw with left hand.
Perform lateral dislocation of the patella and patellar ligament with forceps.
Hold the hind paw gently to avoid trauma in the paw.
Drip sterile saline on the surface of articular cartilage during operation.
Cut through the medial meniscotibial ligament using a No. 10 surgical blade, avoiding injury to the cartilage beneath the medial meniscus.
Identify and cut the meniscotibial ligament connecting the lateral side of the medial meniscus with the intercondylar eminence of the tibia.
Hold the hind paw gently and pull the fat pad aside if necessary to identify the ligament without removing it.
Close the knee joint capsule with a 6-0 absorbable suture.
Close the skin with a 6-0 silk suture.
Apply one drop of 0.25% bupivacaine at the surgical site in each mouse.
Allow operated mice free access to water and food post-surgery.
Fix entire knee joints, decalcified and embedded in paraffin for histological analysis after sacrifice at indicated time points (e.g., 4 weeks, 8 weeks, 12 weeks).
Cut the whole hind limbs using No. 10 blades.
Dissect skin and muscles carefully from the hind limbs.
Fix samples with 4% PFA for 3 days at room temperature.
Remove the PFA from the samples.
Clean the samples with water.
Decalcify the samples in EDTA at 4 °C for 2 weeks.
Keep the samples in 70% ethanol for 1 hour.
Change the ethanol and keep the samples in a new set of 70% ethanol overnight.
Put the samples in 80% ethanol for 1 hour.
Put the samples in 90% ethanol for 1 hour.
Put the samples in 100% ethanol overnight.
Remove the ethanol from the samples.
Keep the samples in xylene for 1 hour.
Change to a new set of xylene and repeat this step 3 times.
Embed the samples into a paraffin mold using the Leica embedding center.
Section the samples at 5 μm using a rotary microtome (Leica RM2255, Germany).
Collect the sections onto glass slides.
Deparaffinize the slides in xylene.
Hydrate the slides in an ethanol gradient to distilled water.
Stain the slides through Weigert's Iron Hematoxylin Solution.
Stain the slides with 0.05% Fast Green (FCF) Solution.
Stain the slides with 1% Acetic Acid Solution.
Stain the slides with 0.1% Safranin O Solution.
Mount the slides using resinous medium.
Perform scoring and statistical analysis through the OARSI scoring system.
Score the Safranin O stained slides based on loss of proteoglycan (red color) in cartilage and percentage of destruction in cartilage structure.
Conduct statistical analysis for the histological score.
